dedupe_keys.name: annual 30 m maps of global grassland class and extent 2000 to 2022 cultivated and natural grassland

description: This Land & Carbon Lab product maps grassland worldwide every year from 2000 to 2022 at 30 m, split into cultivated grassland and natural or semi-natural grassland. Grassland means land with at least 30 per cent low grass and forb cover and limited trees, shrubs and cropland. The maps come from per-class random forest models on bi-monthly GLAD Landsat ARD-2 composites with climate, landform and proximity covariates, trained on over 2.3 million reference samples interpreted in very high resolution imagery; the reference samples are a separate deposit of GeoPackage files. Outputs are two class probability maps and a dominant class map, as Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs on Zenodo and Resource Watch layers, free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence, described in Scientific Data (2024). No updates are planned. Caveats: the provider notes that many areas predicted as cultivated grassland are actually cropland or other cyclical short vegetation, and the paper lists regions of under- and over-prediction. For simulation it gives the extent and change of pasture and rangeland for livestock exposure to drought, wildfire and heat, and for land-use change scenarios. Related catalogue records include the gridded livestock distribution maps and Dynamic World.
